/locations/brampton.question: Where can I find a licensed immigration consultant in Brampton?
/locations/brampton.answer: Commonwealth Migration Group (CMG) has an office at Bovaird Dr E in Brampton, Ontario, with licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC). If you are searching for an immigration consultant near me in Brampton, you can book a consultation to discuss Express Entry, sponsorship, study and work permits, visas and refusals.

/locations/brampton.question: How do I check that an immigration consultant in Brampton is licensed?
/locations/brampton.answer: Search the public register of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) by name or licence number. A licensed RCIC will appear with an active status. Ask any Brampton immigration consultant for their licence number before you pay or sign anything, and never accept a consultant who cannot give one.

/locations/brampton.question: What is the difference between a Brampton RCIC and an immigration lawyer?
/locations/brampton.answer: An RCIC is regulated by the CICC and focuses on immigration and citizenship applications. A lawyer is regulated by the Law Society of Ontario and can also represent you in Federal Court. For most applications, such as Express Entry, sponsorship or permits, a licensed RCIC in Brampton is qualified to advise and represent you before IRCC.

/locations/brampton.question: What immigration services does CMG offer at its Bovaird Drive office in Brampton?
/locations/brampton.answer: CMG supports Express Entry and Canada PR, Ontario nominee applications, spousal sponsorship, Super Visa and parent sponsorship, study permits and PGWP, work permits and LMIA, visitor visas, citizenship, PR card renewal, and refusal responses. These immigration services in Brampton are delivered under the supervision of a licensed RCIC.

/locations/brampton.question: Do you help clients in Mississauga, Caledon and the rest of Peel Region?
/locations/brampton.answer: Yes. Many people searching for an immigration consultant in Peel Region or Mississauga and Brampton work with us. CMG advises clients across Brampton, Bramalea, Mississauga, Caledon and the wider GTA, and can also assist people who are still outside Canada.

/locations/brampton.question: How do I book an appointment with an immigration consultant near me in Brampton?
/locations/brampton.answer: Submit a consultation request through the booking page on this website or contact CMG directly; the team will confirm an available time. Tell us your country, your current status in Canada and the program you are considering. This helps the RCIC prepare so that your first meeting focuses on your actual options rather than general information.

/locations/brampton.question: What should I bring to my first immigration consultation in Brampton?
/locations/brampton.answer: Bring your passport, any current Canadian permits or visas, past IRCC letters or refusals, education and work history, language test results and details of family members. For a refusal, bring the full refusal letter. The more complete your documents, the more precisely a Brampton RCIC can assess your options.

/locations/brampton.question: How much does an immigration consultant cost in Brampton, Ontario?
/locations/brampton.answer: Professional fees depend on the program and the complexity of your file, so there is no single price. A licensed consultant must give you a written service agreement that sets out the fee and services before work begins. Government fees are separate and are paid to IRCC. Ask for the full cost in writing before you commit.

/locations/brampton.question: Can an immigration consultant in Brampton guarantee my visa or PR?
/locations/brampton.answer: No. Only IRCC decides applications, and no licensed consultant can guarantee a visa, permit or permanent residence. Be cautious of anyone who promises a result or claims a special relationship with officers. A good RCIC will explain your chances honestly, including the risks, and prepare the strongest application the facts allow.

/locations/brampton.question: Do I need an immigration consultant, or can I apply to IRCC myself?
/locations/brampton.answer: You can apply on your own because IRCC does not require you to hire a representative. Many people hire a licensed RCIC in Brampton when the case is complex, such as prior refusals, gaps in work history, inadmissibility or tight deadlines. If you use one, they must be named on your application through the Use of Representative form.

/locations/brampton.question: What are the warning signs of an immigration scam in Brampton and Ontario?
/locations/brampton.answer: Warning signs include guaranteed results, requests for cash with no receipt, selling job offers, fake LMIAs, and consultants who cannot show a CICC licence. Only licensed RCICs, lawyers, paralegals and Quebec notaries may charge for immigration advice in Canada. Check the CICC register and report suspected fraud to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

/locations/brampton.question: Can I get help from a Brampton immigration consultant if I am still outside Canada?
/locations/brampton.answer: Yes. Many CMG clients apply from abroad for visitor visas, study permits, work permits, Super Visas and Express Entry. A Brampton immigration consultant can review your profile, prepare your documents and communicate with you online, so you do not need to be in Ontario to start.

/locations/brampton.question: Which immigration programs do Brampton families ask about most?
/locations/brampton.answer: Brampton and Peel Region residents commonly ask about spousal sponsorship, Super Visas for parents, study permits and PGWP for students, work permits, Express Entry and the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program. Each has its own page on this site with eligibility, documents and common refusal reasons.

/locations/brampton.question: Can a licensed immigration consultant represent me before IRCC and CBSA?
/locations/brampton.answer: Yes. A licensed RCIC can represent you before IRCC, the Canada Border Services Agency and the Immigration and Refugee Board. An RCIC cannot represent you in Federal Court. If your case needs judicial review, a consultant should refer you to an immigration lawyer promptly because the deadlines are short.

/locations/brampton.question: What happens after my consultation with CMG in Brampton?
/locations/brampton.answer: If you decide to proceed, you receive a written service agreement, a document checklist and a timeline. Your RCIC then prepares the forms and supporting evidence, reviews them with you and submits the application. You keep your own IRCC account, and we update you when IRCC responds.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: What does an Express Entry consultant in Brampton do?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: An Express Entry consultant in Brampton reviews your age, education, language results and work history, checks which federal program you qualify for, estimates your CRS score and builds your profile. A licensed RCIC can also prepare your documents for the application stage after an Invitation to Apply.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Do I need a Canada PR consultant in Brampton to apply through Express Entry?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: No. You can create an Express Entry profile and apply yourself. People hire a Canada PR consultant in Brampton to avoid mistakes in NOC selection, work experience letters, language test planning or proof of funds, because errors can lead to refusal or a misrepresentation finding. The choice is yours.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Which programs does Express Entry manage for applicants in Brampton?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: Express Entry manages three federal programs: the Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Canadian Experience Class and the Federal Skilled Trades Program. You enter a profile, receive a Comprehensive Ranking System score and may be invited to apply if your score meets a draw cut-off or you fit a category-based draw. Applicants in Brampton and across Ontario use the same federal system.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: How is my CRS score calculated, and can CRS score help in Brampton raise it?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: The CRS awards points for age, education, English and French ability, Canadian work and study history, and a spouse's factors. Getting CRS score help in Brampton means testing scenarios, such as a higher IELTS or CELPIP band, French results or a provincial nomination, to see which step adds the most points for your profile.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: How can I improve my CRS score while living in Brampton?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: Common ways are retaking a language test for higher bands, adding French, completing an educational credential assessment for foreign education, gaining more skilled Canadian work experience in Ontario, and seeking a provincial nomination such as OINP. Each option takes different time and cost, so compare them before you commit.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: What is a good CRS score for Express Entry if I live in Brampton?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: There is no fixed good score. IRCC sets a different cut-off in every draw depending on the draw type and the number of invitations. A score that is competitive in a French-language or healthcare draw may be too low for a general draw. Review IRCC's recent draw results rather than relying on a single number. Where you live in Ontario does not change the cut-off.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Does my work experience in Brampton or Ontario count for the Canadian Experience Class?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: Yes, if the work was authorized, skilled (TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3) and totals at least 12 months within the last three years. Work in Brampton, Mississauga or anywhere in Canada counts equally. Self-employment and work done without authorization do not count toward the Canadian Experience Class.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: What are category-based Express Entry draws?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: Category-based draws invite candidates with specific attributes, such as strong French-language ability or experience in a priority occupation. IRCC publishes the active categories and updates them regularly. If your profile fits a category, your chance of an invitation can be higher than in a general draw with the same score.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Which language tests are accepted for Express Entry in Ontario?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: For English, IRCC accepts IELTS General Training and CELPIP General. For French, it accepts TEF Canada and TCF Canada. Test results are valid for two years, and they must still be valid when you submit your application. Book early because strong language scores are one of the fastest ways to raise your CRS. Check test availability near Brampton before you plan your timeline.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Do I need an ECA for Express Entry if I studied abroad and now live in Brampton?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: If your education was completed outside Canada, you generally need an Educational Credential Assessment from a designated organization such as WES to claim points for it. Canadian credentials do not need one. Start early, because the assessment can take weeks and requires official documents from your school. This applies even if you already live and work in Brampton.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: How long does an Express Entry profile last, and what happens after an invitation?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: An Express Entry profile is valid for 12 months. If you receive an Invitation to Apply, you have 60 days to submit a complete application with all supporting documents. If you miss the deadline, the invitation expires. Prepare documents before you are invited so that you can file on time.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: What documents do I need for Express Entry as a Brampton applicant?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: You typically need a valid passport, language test results, an educational credential assessment, work reference letters, police certificates, an immigration medical exam and proof of funds if required. Reference letters must show duties, hours, pay and dates. A Brampton RCIC can check them against the NOC before you submit.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: How long does Express Entry processing take for applicants in Brampton?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: IRCC aims to process most complete Express Entry applications within about six months, but actual times change. Delays can come from missing documents, medical or security checks. Check IRCC's current processing times and have your documents ready, since an incomplete application can be returned. Processing does not depend on where in Ontario you live.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Can an Ontario nominee nomination help my Express Entry application?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: Yes, if Ontario nominates you through an Express Entry-linked route and you accept the nomination in your profile, it adds 600 CRS points. The current Ontario Workforce Priority stream allows eligible applicants in TEER 0–3 occupations to request an Express Entry-linked nomination if they meet federal criteria. Ontario’s former Human Capital Express Entry streams are closed to new applicants.

/immigrate/express-entry.question: Can an Express Entry consultant in Brampton guarantee an invitation to apply?
/immigrate/express-entry.answer: No. IRCC alone decides who is invited, and cut-offs depend on the pool of candidates. A licensed consultant can improve your profile and prepare your documents, but no one can guarantee an invitation or approval. Avoid any provider who promises a PR outcome or charges for an invitation.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: What is the OINP, and how can an OINP consultant in Ontario help?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: The Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) lets Ontario nominate people for permanent residence based on skills, experience or a job offer. An OINP consultant in Ontario checks which stream fits your profile, prepares the application, and explains what happens after nomination, when you must apply to IRCC for PR.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Do I need to live in Brampton or Ontario to apply to the OINP?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: You must intend to live in Ontario if nominated. Under the current Ontario Workforce Priority stream, most applicants need a qualifying Ontario job offer; eligible self-employed physicians may apply without one. The former Human Capital streams are closed to new applicants. Check Ontario’s current stream criteria and intake before applying.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Which OINP streams can a Brampton applicant use?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Ontario redesigned the OINP in 2026. The current Ontario Workforce Priority stream has pathways for skilled workers with qualifying Ontario job offers and for eligible self-employed physicians. The former Employer Job Offer, Human Capital, Express Entry, graduate, Skilled Trades and Entrepreneur streams are closed to new applicants; applications already submitted are assessed under the rules that applied when filed. Check the official OINP page for current criteria and intake.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: What is the difference between Employer Job Offer and Human Capital streams?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Those were separate parts of Ontario’s former program structure, and they are closed to new applicants. The current Ontario Workforce Priority stream has a job-offer pathway for eligible skilled workers and a separate pathway for eligible self-employed physicians. Review the current criteria before deciding which route applies.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Can a job offer from a Brampton employer help me get nominated?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: A qualifying job offer from an Ontario employer may support an application under the current Ontario Workforce Priority stream. The employer must start the process through Ontario’s Employer Portal, and the candidate must meet the stream’s work experience, language, education and other criteria. Eligible self-employed physicians have a separate route. Employers cannot charge workers for a job offer.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: How does the OINP notification process work for Express Entry candidates in Brampton?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Ontario’s former Human Capital streams and their Notification of Interest process are closed to new applicants. Under the current Workforce Priority stream, an employer starts the job-offer process and the candidate registers an Expression of Interest; Ontario selects candidates and issues invitations based on current priorities. Eligible TEER 0–3 applicants may opt for an Express Entry nomination if they also meet federal criteria. An eligible invitation is not guaranteed.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: How does an Ontario nomination affect my CRS score?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: A nomination linked to your Express Entry profile adds 600 CRS points, which in practice places you well above most draw cut-offs. You are then invited to apply for permanent residence to IRCC. This is why many candidates with moderate CRS scores explore an Ontario PNP consultant in Brampton.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Do I need a job offer from a Brampton employer for the OINP?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: For the current Ontario Workforce Priority stream, most skilled-worker applicants need a qualifying job offer from an Ontario employer. Eligible self-employed physicians may apply through a separate pathway without a job offer. Ontario’s former Employer Job Offer and Human Capital streams are closed to new applicants, so check the current rules before applying.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Is there a minimum language level for OINP streams?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Language requirements depend on the current Ontario Workforce Priority pathway and the occupation’s TEER category. Check Ontario’s current eligibility page for the required Canadian Language Benchmark in each ability before registering an Expression of Interest. A stronger language result can also affect your federal options.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: How long does an OINP application take for Brampton applicants?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Processing time varies by stream and volume, so check the OINP website for current times. After nomination, you must apply to IRCC for permanent residence, which has its own processing time, medical exam and background checks. Plan for both stages when you think about work permits and timelines. Where you live in Ontario does not change processing times.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Can an OINP consultant in Ontario check whether my job offer is genuine?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: A licensed RCIC can review the offer letter, the employer's documents and the wage against OINP requirements to spot problems. Be cautious of anyone selling job offers or asking you to pay an employer. OINP rules prohibit this, and a fraudulent offer can lead to refusal or a misrepresentation finding.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: What can I do if my Ontario PNP application from Brampton is refused?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Review the refusal reasons carefully. You may be able to apply again if you fix the problem, apply under another stream, or build a stronger Express Entry profile. Do not submit a second application with the same weaknesses. A Brampton RCIC can compare options before you spend more time and money.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: What is the difference between the OINP and Express Entry?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Express Entry is a federal system that ranks eligible candidates for permanent residence. The OINP is Ontario’s nomination program, and IRCC makes the final PR decision. Under the current Ontario Workforce Priority stream, eligible TEER 0–3 applicants may request an Express Entry-linked nomination if they also meet federal criteria; other nominations use a non-Express Entry process. An Express Entry-linked provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Can a Brampton RCIC help if my occupation is in skilled trades?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: Ontario’s former Express Entry Skilled Trades stream is closed to new applicants. A tradesperson may still qualify under the current Ontario Workforce Priority stream if they meet its requirements, including a qualifying Ontario job offer, or may consider a federal or other provincial route. A licensed RCIC can review your occupation code, duties and credentials against the current criteria.

/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.question: Can an OINP consultant in Ontario guarantee that I will be nominated?
/immigrate/ontario-pnp-oinp.answer: No. Ontario decides nominations and can change criteria and intake at any time. A licensed consultant can check your eligibility, prepare a strong application and manage deadlines, but cannot guarantee a nomination or permanent residence. Avoid anyone who promises nomination or asks for payment for a spot.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What is spousal sponsorship in Canada, and who can sponsor?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Spousal sponsorship Canada lets a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, aged 18 or older, sponsor a spouse, common-law partner or conjugal partner for permanent residence. The sponsor signs an undertaking to support the partner financially. A spousal sponsorship consultant in Brampton can check whether you meet the sponsor and relationship rules.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Who can I sponsor as a partner if I live in Brampton?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: You can sponsor a legally married spouse, a common-law partner who has lived with you for at least 12 consecutive months, or a conjugal partner who could not live with you or marry because of serious legal or immigration barriers. Each category has different evidence requirements, so choose the right one from the start. Sponsors living in Brampton and elsewhere in Ontario follow the same federal rules.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What is the difference between inland and outland spousal sponsorship?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Inland sponsorship is for couples living together in Canada, where the partner has valid temporary status. Outland sponsorship is for a partner living abroad, or for couples who want to process through a visa office. Each route affects where your spouse can live, travel and work during processing. Many Brampton couples compare both before applying.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Can my spouse live and work in Brampton while the application is processing?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: If you apply inland and your partner is already in Canada with valid status, an open work permit may be available while the application is processed. For outland applications, your partner generally waits abroad unless they qualify to visit or hold another status. Confirm the current rules before making travel plans.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What financial requirements apply when sponsoring a spouse in Ontario?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: For a spouse or partner, there is generally no minimum income requirement, but you must sign an undertaking that commits you to support your partner for three years after they become a permanent resident. You cannot sponsor if you receive certain social assistance, unless it is due to disability. Other limits can apply, so review your situation. Quebec has separate undertaking rules, but Ontario sponsors follow the federal requirements.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What documents prove a genuine relationship in a Brampton spousal sponsorship?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Evidence can include your marriage certificate, photos over time, travel records, shared lease or mortgage, joint bank accounts, messages and call logs, and statements from family and friends. Officers look at the whole story, so quality and consistency matter more than volume. A consultant can help you organize evidence logically.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: How long does spousal sponsorship Canada take for couples in Brampton?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Processing time varies by whether you apply inland or outland and by the country, case volume and completeness of the application. IRCC publishes current processing times and updates them regularly. Prepare a complete application with a clear relationship timeline, since missing documents can cause delays or refusal. Brampton couples should check IRCC's current times before making plans.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Why do spousal sponsorship applications from Brampton couples get refused?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Typical reasons include doubts that the relationship is genuine, inconsistent answers or timelines, insufficient evidence, inadmissibility such as criminality or medical issues, and past misrepresentation. If refused, review the reasons carefully. You may have appeal rights as a sponsor, so act within the deadline.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Can I sponsor a new spouse if I was sponsored before or had a previous partner?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: There are restrictions. If you were sponsored as a spouse and became a permanent resident, you generally cannot sponsor a new spouse for five years. Similar limits apply if you previously sponsored a spouse who has become a permanent resident. These rules can be complex, so get your history reviewed before you apply.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Is my marriage valid for Canadian immigration if it took place abroad, as with many Brampton couples?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: A marriage must be legally valid where it took place and under Canadian law. Many Brampton couples married overseas or in religious ceremonies, and these can qualify if legal requirements were met. Proxy, telephone or other special marriages need careful review before you apply.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Will criminal history or a medical condition stop my spouse's application?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Not automatically. Criminality, medical issues and prior immigration violations can make someone inadmissible, but solutions may exist depending on the facts, such as rehabilitation, a pardon or a waiver. Disclose all history honestly because misrepresentation can lead to a five-year ban. A consultant can review the risk early.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What medical, police and biometric steps are required?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Your partner will generally need an immigration medical exam with an approved panel physician, police certificates from relevant countries and biometrics. IRCC will tell you when to complete each step. Starting police certificates early can save weeks, because some countries take a long time to issue them.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Can dependent children be included in my spousal sponsorship from Brampton?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: Yes. Dependent children of the sponsored partner can usually be included if they meet the age and dependency rules. Children must be listed on the application even if they are not immigrating, or they may be barred later. Review the family composition carefully before filing.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: What are my responsibilities after my spouse becomes a permanent resident?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: As a sponsor you remain financially responsible for your partner for the three-year undertaking period, even if the relationship ends. This does not stop your partner from working, but it does mean you must repay certain government benefits if they claim social assistance. Understand this commitment before you sign.

/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.question: Can a spousal sponsorship consultant in Brampton guarantee approval?
/sponsor/spousal-and-partner-sponsorship.answer: No. IRCC makes the final decision, and no licensed consultant can guarantee approval or timelines. What a spousal sponsorship consultant in Brampton can do is review eligibility, prepare strong evidence and help you respond to requests. If a sponsorship is refused, appeal rights and deadlines can be short, so seek advice immediately.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: What is the Super Visa, and how can a Super Visa consultant in Brampton help?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: The Super Visa is a multiple-entry visa for parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, letting them visit for extended periods. A Super Visa consultant in Brampton checks your income, prepares the invitation letter and insurance evidence, and reviews your parents' documents to reduce the risk of refusal.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Who can apply for a Super Visa to visit family in Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: The applicant must be the parent or grandparent of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and the child or grandchild must provide an invitation letter, proof of income and a commitment of support. The applicant must also pass the medical exam and hold qualifying Canadian medical insurance. The host can live anywhere in Canada, including Brampton and Peel Region.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: What income does my child or grandchild in Brampton need to show?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: The host must meet IRCC’s minimum necessary income for the family size. Since March 31, 2026, hosts may qualify using the income requirement from either of the two preceding tax years; in some cases, the visiting parent’s or grandparent’s income can make up the remaining amount if the host and co-signer meet the required minimum share. Check IRCC’s current table and evidence rules.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Can my spouse's income be included for the Super Visa income test?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Yes. The host’s spouse or common-law partner may co-sign the invitation and have their income included. Since March 31, 2026, the visiting parent’s or grandparent’s income may also be added to cover part of the requirement if the host and co-signer meet the minimum share set by IRCC. The host may use qualifying income from either of the two taxation years before applying; check current evidence rules.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: What medical insurance do my parents need to visit me in Brampton on a Super Visa?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Each parent needs private health insurance that covers health care, hospitalization and repatriation, provides at least $100,000 in emergency coverage, and is valid for at least one year from the date of entry. It may be issued by a Canadian insurance company or an eligible foreign company authorized to provide insurance in Canada. The policy must be paid as required by IRCC; a quote alone is not enough.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Do my parents need an immigration medical exam for the Super Visa?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Yes. Parents must complete an immigration medical exam with an IRCC-approved panel physician. You can do the exam before submitting the application, which may speed things up. Results are valid for a limited time, so plan the exam close to your application date.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: What should the invitation letter say for a Super Visa from Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: The letter should state your relationship, your parents' details, your Brampton address and contact information, the planned length of visit, and your commitment to provide financial support. Attach proof of your status as a citizen or permanent resident. Keep the letter consistent with the rest of the application.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: What documents are needed for a Super Visa application in Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Typical documents include passports, proof of relationship, the invitation letter, the host's income evidence, proof of status, insurance proof, a medical exam confirmation, photos and biometrics. Some applicants also include evidence of ties to their home country. A checklist from a Brampton consultant keeps the package complete.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: How long can my parents stay with me in Brampton on a Super Visa?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: A Super Visa can be valid for up to ten years, and parents can usually stay up to five years at a time on each entry. The officer decides the length of the visit at the border. Parents can apply to extend inside Canada, so plan for insurance validity throughout their stay.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Super Visa or visitor visa: which is better for parents visiting Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: A regular visitor visa is generally for visits of six months or less and does not have the Super Visa’s host-income threshold or mandatory one-year insurance rule. A Super Visa can allow a longer stay, but requires host income evidence, qualifying insurance and a medical exam. Both are temporary visas, and applicants must meet the relevant visitor requirements.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Can my parents work or use OHIP in Ontario while on a Super Visa?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: No. A Super Visa does not allow work, and holders generally do not qualify for OHIP, so private medical insurance is important. Parents can visit, stay with family and travel in and out of Canada. If they want to work or settle permanently, other immigration options must be considered.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Why do Super Visa applications get refused, and what can I do?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Common reasons include insufficient host income, insurance that does not meet requirements, missing documents, concern that parents will not leave, or medical inadmissibility. Request the officer's notes and correct the problems before reapplying. A Super Visa application help service in Brampton can review the refusal and your strongest next step.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Should my parents apply for a Super Visa or the Parents and Grandparents Program?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: They are different. The Super Visa is a temporary visa for extended visits. The Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) can lead to permanent residence but has limited intake and a selection process. Many Brampton families use the Super Visa while waiting or deciding whether to sponsor. See our PGP page for details.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Can my parents apply from outside Canada while I live in Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Yes. Parents usually apply from their home country, and you can prepare the invitation letter and financial documents from Brampton. They must provide biometrics at the designated centre. Processing times vary by country, so apply well before the planned trip and check IRCC's current times.

/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.question: Can I reapply for a Super Visa after a refusal if I live in Brampton?
/visit/super-visa-standalone-page.answer: Yes, but a new application should fix the reasons for the refusal rather than repeat it. Request the officer's notes, then correct issues such as host income, insurance, documents or ties. A Brampton RCIC can review the refusal and decide whether to reapply, add evidence or consider another option such as a visitor visa.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: What does a study permit consultant in Brampton do?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: A study permit consultant in Brampton reviews your school offer, funds, study plan and immigration history, then prepares a strong application. A licensed RCIC can also help with letters of explanation, refusals and changes to your permit. The aim is a clear, consistent file that shows you are a genuine student.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Who needs a study permit to study in Brampton or elsewhere in Canada?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Most international students need a study permit for programs longer than six months. Some people, such as certain family members of diplomats, are exempt. You must first receive a letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution (DLI). Check that your school and program are eligible before you pay tuition.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: What documents are required for a Canada study permit application in Brampton?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: You will typically need a valid passport, a letter of acceptance from a DLI, a provincial attestation letter if required, proof of funds, a study plan or letter of explanation, a medical exam if requested, police certificates and biometrics. A Brampton consultant can build a checklist for your country and program.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Do I need a Provincial Attestation Letter for Ontario?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Most new study permit applicants need a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL), which an Ontario institution issues after you accept an offer. Some programs and groups are exempt under federal rules. Rules have changed several times, so confirm the requirement for your program before you apply.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: How much money do I need to show for a study permit if I plan to live in Brampton?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: You must show enough funds to pay tuition, living costs for yourself and any family members, and return travel. IRCC sets the minimum living cost amount and updates it. Funds are commonly shown through bank statements, a GIC and a sponsor letter. Show the source of the money clearly. Plan realistically for living costs in the Greater Toronto Area.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Why are study permits refused in Canada?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Common reasons include doubts that you will leave Canada after your studies, a weak or unclear study plan, insufficient funds, unexplained gaps, previous refusals and incomplete documents. A refusal letter lists the reasons. A study permit refusal in Brampton calls for a careful review before any new application.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: What should I do after a study permit refusal in Brampton?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Read the refusal letter, request the officer's notes, and decide whether to reapply with stronger evidence, fix the problem such as funds or study plan, or choose another school or program. Reapplying without addressing the reasons often leads to another refusal. Judicial review is a legal remedy with short deadlines.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Can I work while studying in Brampton or elsewhere in Ontario?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Many full-time students at designated institutions can work off campus for a limited number of hours per week during academic sessions, and full-time during scheduled breaks. Co-op placements require a co-op work permit. Always check the conditions on your permit, since working beyond them can affect your status.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Can my spouse or children come with me to Canada as a student?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Often yes, but an open work permit for a spouse is limited to certain programs, such as some master's and doctoral programs. Children may qualify for visitor status or study permits. Rules changed recently, so verify your spouse's eligibility before you move the family.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Can I extend my study permit or change schools while living in Brampton?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: You can apply to extend your permit before it expires if you are still studying. If you change schools, you may need to inform IRCC, and a different DLI must be on the approved list. Maintain full-time enrolment and good standing to protect your status and later work permit options.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Which schools near Brampton accept international students?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Options in Brampton and Peel include Sheridan's Davis Campus in Brampton and other colleges and universities across the Greater Toronto Area. Whichever school you choose, confirm it is a designated learning institution on IRCC's list and that your program is eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Do I need an English test for a Canada study permit?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: IRCC does not set a universal language test for the study permit itself, but most schools require IELTS, TOEFL or another accepted test for admission. A strong language score also supports your study plan. If you plan to apply for PGWP or PR later, your language results matter even more.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: How long does a study permit application take?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: Processing times depend on your country and the time of year, and IRCC publishes current estimates. Apply as soon as you have your acceptance letter and PAL, and do not wait for term start dates. Missing documents and biometrics are common causes of delay.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Can I apply for a study permit from inside Canada?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: In most cases you apply from outside Canada, but some people already in Canada, such as certain permit holders, may be able to apply inside the country. Changing from a visitor to a student has restrictions. Check your status before applying, because an incorrect route can lead to refusal.

/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.question: Can a study permit consultant in Brampton guarantee approval?
/work-and-study/canada-study-permit.answer: No. IRCC officers make the decision and no licensed consultant can guarantee a study permit. A consultant can strengthen your file by reviewing funds, the study plan and the school choice, and by catching issues that cause refusals. Be careful of anyone who guarantees admission or a permit.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: What is a PGWP, and how can PGWP application help in Brampton assist me?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: A Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) lets eligible international graduates work in Canada after finishing a program. PGWP application help in Brampton includes checking your program, language results and timelines, preparing documents, and making sure you apply on time to protect your work authorization.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Who is eligible for a PGWP after graduating from a Brampton or Ontario college?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: You generally must have graduated from an eligible program at a designated learning institution, studied full time, maintained status, and meet language and, for some college programs, field-of-study requirements. Not every program leads to a PGWP, so confirm eligibility before choosing a school, ideally before you pay tuition. The same federal rules apply to graduates of Brampton, Peel and other Ontario institutions.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: How long is a PGWP valid for graduates in Brampton?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: The validity usually matches your program length, up to a maximum of three years. A program of at least two years can qualify for a three-year permit, while shorter programs get a permit of similar length to the program. Your program duration is counted from your official completion letter.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: When should I apply for a PGWP after graduating in Brampton?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: You must apply within 180 days of receiving your final marks or written confirmation that you completed your program. Missing this window can end your eligibility. Request your official transcript and completion letter early, since delays at the school can eat into your 180 days.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can I work in Brampton while my PGWP application is in process?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: You may be able to work full time if you applied before your study permit expired, held authorization to work off campus, and completed your program. Do not assume you can work. Check the current IRCC rules for your situation, since working without authorization can harm your future PR plans.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: What language test do I need for a PGWP if I studied in Ontario?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Recent rules require language proof for most PGWP applicants, with a higher level for university graduates than for college graduates. Approved tests include IELTS, CELPIP and, for French, TEF or TCF. Check the current minimum levels and book your test early so that results are ready when you apply.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Does my college program need to be on the field-of-study list?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: For many college programs, IRCC requires that the field of study be on a published list linked to labour market needs. University degree programs are generally treated differently. Check the list before you enrol, because a program that does not qualify could leave you without a PGWP after graduation.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can I apply for a PGWP from outside Canada?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Yes, within the 180-day window you can apply from outside Canada, as long as you meet the criteria. If you leave Canada, plan carefully for travel and entry. A Brampton RCIC can explain the effects on your status and work rights, depending on your study permit expiry.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: What documents are required for a PGWP application from Brampton?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: You will need your passport, study permit, official transcript, completion letter from your school, language test results if required, photos and the fee. Make sure the program dates on your letter match your records. Inconsistent dates are a common reason for delays and refusals.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Why are PGWP applications refused, and how can a Brampton RCIC help?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Common reasons include applying after the 180-day deadline, graduating from an ineligible program, not meeting the language requirement, having a gap in full-time enrolment or not holding valid status. Request your refusal reasons, then compare options such as a restoration application or other work permits.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can part-time or online studies qualify for a PGWP?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Strict rules apply. Studying part time or mostly online can reduce your PGWP eligibility or length. Check the rules for your intake date and program, and ask your school for written confirmation of your enrolment history. Planning before your final term is far easier than fixing a problem afterward.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can I apply for PR after a PGWP?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Yes. After PGWP, many graduates gain 12 months of skilled Canadian work experience and become eligible for the Canadian Experience Class under Express Entry, or consider the OINP. Work in Brampton counts as Canadian experience if the job is skilled and authorized. Plan your job and language results early.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can I extend my PGWP while working in Brampton?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: A PGWP is generally issued only once and cannot be extended in the usual way. Limited exceptions exist, such as an expiring passport. Because of this, start planning your next step, such as a work permit or PR pathway, well before your PGWP ends.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: Can I get more than one PGWP?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: Usually not. You can generally get only one PGWP in your lifetime, even if you complete more than one program. That is why choosing the right program and timing matters, and why you should confirm your program is PGWP-eligible before you enrol. Check current exceptions with your RCIC.

/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.question: What does a PGWP cost, and how long does it take?
/work-and-study/post-graduation-work-per.answer: The government fee is set by IRCC and is separate from any consultant fee. Processing time varies and changes frequently, so check IRCC's current estimate when you apply. Applying early within your 180-day window and submitting complete documents helps you avoid delays.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: What is an LMIA, and when does a Brampton employer need one?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: A Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) is issued by Employment and Social Development Canada and shows that hiring a foreign worker will not harm the local labour market. LMIA for employers in Brampton is needed when the job is not covered by an LMIA-exempt work permit option. A positive LMIA is usually followed by a work permit application.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: How can an LMIA consultant in Ontario help my business?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: An LMIA consultant in Ontario reviews whether the position qualifies, checks wages against requirements, plans compliant advertising, prepares the application and supports the worker's later work permit. A licensed RCIC can also advise you on alternatives that do not need an LMIA, which may save time and cost.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: How much is the LMIA fee for Brampton employers, and who pays it?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: The government processing fee is $1,000 per position, and the employer pays it. The employer cannot recover this fee or any recruitment cost from the worker. Charging a worker for an LMIA or a job offer is not permitted and can lead to penalties. Always keep clear written records.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: What is the difference between the high-wage and low-wage LMIA streams?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Positions are classified by comparing the offered hourly wage with the provincial or territorial median wage. High-wage positions usually require a transition plan, while low-wage positions have limits such as caps on the share of low-wage workers. Check the current median wage for Ontario before you set the wage.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: What recruitment must a Brampton employer do before applying for an LMIA?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Employers generally must advertise the job in Canada for a minimum period, including on the Job Bank and using additional methods, and show that no suitable Canadian or permanent resident was available. Keep records of ads, applicants and reasons for rejection. Gaps in recruitment evidence are a common cause of refusal.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Do I need a transition plan for a high-wage LMIA?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Most high-wage LMIA applications require a transition plan describing how you will reduce reliance on temporary foreign workers over time, for example through training or hiring Canadians. The plan should be realistic and specific to your business. A generic plan can weaken the application.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Which Brampton industries commonly use LMIAs?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Brampton and Peel Region employers in manufacturing, logistics and trucking, food processing, hospitality, construction and health care often explore LMIAs. Eligibility depends on the specific job, wage and the current rules for each stream. Your RCIC can tell you whether an LMIA is realistic for your position.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Can low-wage LMIA applications be refused in the Brampton and Peel area?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Yes. Low-wage LMIA applications may be refused processing in regions where the unemployment rate exceeds a set threshold. Check the current list for your region before you advertise or apply. If your area is affected, you may need to consider different hiring options. Ask your consultant whether the Brampton area is currently affected.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: How long does an LMIA take for an Ontario employer?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Processing time depends on the stream, the volume and the quality of your application. ESDC publishes current estimates, and a complete application with strong recruitment evidence moves more smoothly. Plan for the LMIA stage and then the worker's work permit, since both add time before the person can start work.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: What happens after a positive LMIA is issued?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: The employer gives the worker a copy of the positive LMIA and a job offer. The worker then applies to IRCC for a work permit tied to that employer. The LMIA has a limited validity period, so the worker should apply promptly. The permit conditions will match the job offered.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Why do LMIAs get refused for Brampton employers?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Common reasons include a wage below the required level, incomplete or inadequate recruitment, a job offer that does not look genuine, a business that cannot show it can pay the wage and a poor compliance record. A refusal letter explains the reasons. Fix them before reapplying.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: What are my obligations as an employer after hiring a foreign worker?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: You must provide the wages, hours and duties promised in the offer, keep records, follow employment standards and allow inspections. Changing the job, wage or location without proper approval can cause compliance problems. A licensed consultant can help you set up record-keeping and prepare for an inspection.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Are there ways to hire a foreign worker in Ontario without an LMIA?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: Yes. Some work permits are LMIA-exempt, such as certain intra-company transfers, CUSMA professionals, Francophone Mobility and open work permits like PGWP. Some require the employer to submit an offer through the IRCC Employer Portal and pay a compliance fee. Your consultant can check which exemption applies.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Can a worker in Brampton be asked to pay for a job offer or LMIA?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: No. Employers cannot charge workers for an LMIA or for the job offer, and anyone selling job offers or LMIAs is committing fraud. Workers who pay for these often end up with refused applications and lost money. Report suspicious offers and check the offer with a licensed consultant.

/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.question: Does a positive LMIA still add CRS points for Express Entry?
/work-and-study/lmia-and-employer-servic.answer: A positive LMIA does not currently add CRS points. IRCC removed job-offer CRS points on March 25, 2025. Starting November 3, 2026, IRCC plans to award points for qualifying high-wage job offers under a new formula; an LMIA alone will not provide points. A job offer may still matter for Federal Skilled Worker eligibility, a work permit or a provincial stream, so check the rule in effect when you apply.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: What does a visitor visa consultant in Brampton do?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: A visitor visa consultant in Brampton reviews the purpose of travel, the applicant's finances, family and work ties and past travel history, then prepares a clear application and letter of explanation. A licensed RCIC can also review refusals and prepare a stronger reapplication.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Who needs a temporary resident visa, and who needs only an eTA?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Citizens of many countries need a temporary resident visa (TRV) to visit Canada, while citizens of visa-exempt countries need only an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) when flying. Check the rules for your passport on IRCC's website. Having an eTA or TRV does not guarantee entry, which is decided by the border officer.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: How do I write an invitation letter for relatives visiting me in Brampton?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: An invitation letter should include your name, address and status in Canada, your relationship with the visitor, the purpose and dates of the visit, where they will stay and who covers costs. Attach proof of status and income if relevant. An invitation letter for Canada in Brampton helps, but it does not guarantee a visa.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: What documents do I need for a Canada visitor visa when my host lives in Brampton?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Typical documents include a valid passport, a completed application, proof of funds, employment or business documents, proof of family ties, previous travel history, itinerary and an invitation letter if visiting family. Biometrics are required for most applicants. Provide clear, recent documents.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Why was my visitor visa refused for Canada when my family lives in Brampton?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Common reasons include insufficient proof of funds, weak ties to your home country, an unclear purpose of travel, limited travel history, incomplete documents and previous immigration issues. The refusal letter lists checkbox reasons that are often generic, so request the officer's notes for more detail.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Can I reapply immediately after a TRV refusal, and what is TRV refusal help?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: You can reapply, but a new application with the same evidence often gets the same result. TRV refusal help means reviewing the reasons, collecting stronger evidence, explaining any gaps and correcting errors before you submit again. A consultant in Brampton can advise whether to reapply, wait or choose another option.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: How long can my relatives stay in Brampton on a visitor visa?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Visitors are usually allowed to stay up to six months, but the officer at the border decides the length of stay and may give less. Check the date stamped in your passport or on your documents. Staying longer than allowed can affect future applications.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Can a visitor extend their stay while in Brampton?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Yes, a visitor can apply to extend their stay before the current status expires. Apply well before the deadline, show that you have funds and a plan to leave, and keep the same conditions. If you apply in time, you may remain in Canada while IRCC decides, under maintained status.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: How long can a multiple-entry visitor visa be valid?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: A multiple-entry visitor visa can be valid for up to ten years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first. Each visit is limited to the stay allowed at entry, normally up to six months. Officers can issue shorter visas depending on circumstances.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Do visitors to Brampton and the rest of Ontario need health insurance?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: It is not mandatory for every visitor, but it is strongly recommended because visitors are not covered by OHIP and medical costs in Ontario can be high. Super Visa applicants must have insurance. Buy a policy that covers hospitalization and emergency care for the whole stay.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Can I work or study on a visitor visa?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: No. A visitor visa does not authorize work, and study is allowed only for short courses of up to six months. If you plan to work or study longer, you need the right permit. Working without authorization can lead to removal and bans on future applications.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Should my parents apply for a visitor visa or a Super Visa?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: A visitor visa suits shorter trips, while a Super Visa suits longer visits and multiple entries but requires income and insurance proof. Brampton families should compare the length of the planned stay, income of the host and cost of insurance before choosing. See our Super Visa page for more.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Can a Brampton consultant help if I have a previous refusal or overstay on my record?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: You must disclose past refusals and overstays honestly, because hiding them can lead to a misrepresentation finding. Explain what has changed since then, such as stronger finances or ties. A consultant can help you prepare a clear explanation and gather evidence.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: Do I need to buy a return ticket before applying for a visitor visa?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: You do not usually need to buy a non-refundable ticket before the visa is approved. What matters is showing a credible travel plan and that you will leave Canada at the end of your stay, supported by finances, work, family and other ties. Avoid committing to fixed bookings before approval.

/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.question: How can I help my relative's application as a host in Brampton?
/visit/visitor-visa-trv-standalone-page.answer: Provide a clear invitation letter, proof of your status and income, details of where they will stay and what you plan to do together. Hosts should be honest and consistent with the visitor's application. A strong host letter helps, but the visitor still needs their own ties and funds.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What should I do first if I get an immigration refusal in Brampton?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Read the refusal letter carefully and note the deadline for any action. Gather the application you submitted and request the officer's notes. Do not reapply immediately with the same documents. A licensed immigration refusal consultant in Brampton can review the reasons and compare your options, including reapplying, requesting reconsideration or an appeal.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What is a procedural fairness letter, and how does a Brampton RCIC respond to one?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: A procedural fairness letter is a notice from IRCC that raises a concern about your application, such as possible misrepresentation, inadmissibility or doubts about your eligibility, and gives you a chance to respond before a decision. The response you submit can determine the outcome, so treat the deadline seriously.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: How quickly should I contact a Brampton RCIC after a procedural fairness letter?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: The deadline is stated in the letter and is often short. Missing it can lead to a refusal based on the information IRCC already has. If you need more time, you may ask in writing before the deadline, but an extension is not guaranteed. Contact a Brampton RCIC as soon as the letter arrives.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What should a procedural fairness letter response include?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: A strong response answers each concern directly, with a clear explanation, supporting documents and a consistent timeline. A cover letter should be accurate and calm, without guessing or adding new unrelated information. A procedural fairness letter response in Canada must be truthful, because inconsistent statements can create new problems.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What is misrepresentation in Canada, and can a Brampton consultant help?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Misrepresentation means providing false or misleading information, or withholding material facts, that could affect a decision. A finding can lead to a five-year ban on applying to Canada. Even an innocent mistake can trigger a letter, so review your application history before you respond.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What is the difference between reconsideration, reapplying and judicial review?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Reconsideration asks IRCC to look again at an error in the decision. Reapplying means filing a new application with stronger evidence. Judicial review asks the Federal Court to review the legality of the decision and requires a lawyer. Which option is best depends on the reasons for refusal and the deadlines.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What is a reconsideration request in Canada, and can a Brampton RCIC prepare one?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: A reconsideration request asks IRCC to review a decision, usually because of a factual or procedural error, or new information that existed at the time. It is not a general appeal, and IRCC does not have to reconsider. Use it only if the facts support the request.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: How do I get the officer's notes for my refusal?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: You can request your file notes through an Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) request or through the IRCC process for GCMS notes. The notes can show what the officer concluded and why. They are often the key to deciding between reapplying, reconsideration or legal options.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Can I take my refusal to Federal Court from Ontario?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Judicial review in the Federal Court is a legal option, but deadlines are short, generally 15 days for decisions made in Canada and 60 days for decisions made outside Canada. Only a lawyer can represent you in Federal Court. An RCIC will refer you to a lawyer if this is the best route.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Can I appeal an IRCC refusal if I live in Brampton?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Only some decisions can be appealed. For example, a sponsor whose family class application was refused can usually appeal to the Immigration Appeal Division within 30 days. Many other refusals, such as visitor visas and study permits, have no appeal. Check your options right away.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Should I reapply after a refusal?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Sometimes. If the problem can be fixed with better evidence, a new application can succeed. If the refusal was due to inadmissibility or misrepresentation, reapplying without addressing it can make matters worse. Review the reasons first, then decide with your consultant.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Which kinds of refusals can an RCIC in Brampton help with?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: A licensed RCIC can help with refusals of visitor visas, study permits, work permits, permanent residence and sponsorship applications, including reviewing reasons, preparing a new application and responding to procedural fairness letters. Court proceedings require a lawyer, and your RCIC will tell you if that applies.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Will a refusal affect my future applications?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Yes, it can. You must disclose previous refusals on later applications, and officers may review the earlier decision. A refusal does not always prevent future approval, but the new application should address what went wrong. Be honest, because hiding a refusal can lead to a misrepresentation finding.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: What should I bring to a refusal review consultation in Brampton?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: Bring the refusal letter, your full application copy, any IRCC emails or letters, the officer's notes if you have them, supporting documents and a timeline of events. The faster you provide the file, the faster an RCIC can identify the main problem and the realistic next steps.

/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.question: Can a consultant promise to overturn my refusal?
/inadmissibility-and-appeals/refusal-and.answer: No. IRCC and the courts make decisions, and no licensed consultant can promise a result. A consultant can analyze the reasons, point out errors, prepare a stronger submission and meet deadlines. Be wary of anyone who guarantees to overturn a refusal or claims inside influence.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Who is eligible to apply for Canadian citizenship in Brampton?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Generally you must be a permanent resident with no unfulfilled conditions, have been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days in the five years before applying, file taxes if required, pass the language and knowledge requirements if you are 18 to 54, and have no prohibitions such as certain criminal issues.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: How many days must I be in Canada before applying for citizenship?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: You need 1,095 days of physical presence in the five years before the date you apply. Use the IRCC calculator to count days carefully, including trips outside Canada. Applying too early can lead to refusal, so check your count before submitting your citizenship application in Brampton.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Do I have to file taxes to become a citizen?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: If you are required to file taxes, you must have filed for at least three of the five years before applying. Check your records with the Canada Revenue Agency, because missing filings can delay or block your application. Keep copies of your notices of assessment.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What language level is needed for citizenship in Ontario?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Applicants aged 18 to 54 must show Canadian Language Benchmark 4 in English or French for speaking and listening. You can prove it with approved test results, education in English or French, or other accepted documents. Choose the proof that is strongest and easiest to document.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What is on the Canadian citizenship test?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: The test is based on the Discover Canada study guide and covers rights and responsibilities, history, government, symbols and geography. It is usually taken online or in person after IRCC schedules it. Applicants aged 18 to 54 must take it, and you can prepare using IRCC's study materials.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What documents do I need for a citizenship application?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: You will typically need proof of PR status, passport and travel documents, language proof, a list of absences from Canada, tax information and photos. Be consistent in your travel dates. A Brampton citizenship consultant can check your documents against your passport stamps before you submit.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: How long does the citizenship process take for applicants in Brampton?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Processing times vary and IRCC updates its estimates regularly. After you apply, you may receive a test or interview notice, then an oath ceremony date. Delays can occur if documents are missing or your residence days need to be reviewed. Check current times on IRCC's site.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: How are my trips outside Canada counted?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Only days physically in Canada count toward the 1,095-day requirement, so trips abroad reduce your total. Keep passport copies, flight records and a travel log. Inconsistent travel history can trigger a residence questionnaire and delay your application.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What is a residence questionnaire?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: A residence questionnaire is a request from IRCC for detailed proof of where you lived and your time in Canada, when the officer has doubts about your physical presence. You must provide documents such as lease, bills and employment records. Respond carefully and keep your explanations consistent.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Can my children in Brampton become citizens with me?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Children under 18 can apply for citizenship if a parent is a Canadian citizen or is applying, using a separate application for minors. They have different eligibility rules, such as no physical presence requirement. Check your family situation before filing.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Do I need a valid PR card to apply for citizenship?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: You need to be a permanent resident, but an expired PR card does not by itself stop you from applying. Travel by commercial carrier requires a valid PR card or travel document. If your card is expiring, check our PR card renewal page and plan your renewal and citizenship timing together.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Can I hold dual citizenship if I become Canadian?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Canada allows dual citizenship, but your other country may not. Some countries require you to give up your citizenship when you naturalize elsewhere. Check your home country's rules before you apply, especially if you own property or plan to travel on that passport.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What happens at the citizenship oath ceremony for Brampton applicants?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: At the ceremony you take the oath of citizenship, receive your certificate and become a Canadian citizen. IRCC will tell you the format and location. After the ceremony, you can apply for a Canadian passport. Bring the documents listed on your notice and arrive on time.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: Can an immigration consultant in Brampton help with a citizenship application?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: Yes. A licensed RCIC can check your eligibility, count your days, review your taxes and travel history, prepare the application and respond to IRCC requests. Citizenship applications are often simple, but mistakes in the day count or forms can cause long delays. No consultant can guarantee approval.

/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.question: What if my citizenship application is refused or delayed?
/citizenship/adult-grant-of-citizenship.answer: You will receive a decision letter that explains the reasons. Depending on the reasons, you may reapply when eligible, correct errors or consider legal remedies, which have short deadlines. For delays, check IRCC's processing times first, and contact your consultant if the case is outside normal times.
