/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: An open work permit for vulnerable workers may be available. Seek help quickly and keep records. Community organizations can support you.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: What language level did the Home Support Worker Pilot require?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: Requirements depend on the program, often CLB 4 to CLB 5 or higher. Take an approved test early. Residents of Brampton, Mississauga and the wider GTA can have a licensed RCIC confirm this before they file.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: What training is required?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: Training and experience requirements depend on the program and category. The former Home Support Worker Pilot is closed to new applicants; IRCC’s newer Home Care Worker Immigration Pilot had separate education and training criteria, but its intake is paused. Review the official instructions for the exact program and date that apply to you.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: Do I need Ontario registration to work as a PSW?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: Many employers want personal support worker training and certification. Requirements vary by employer and setting. Check before you apply.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: Can my family come with me as a home support worker?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: Family provisions depend on the program and your permit. Check eligibility for your spouse and children. A Brampton RCIC can walk through this step with you and flag anything that needs official confirmation.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: How do I avoid home support worker immigration scams?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: Do not pay for job offers or LMIAs and verify recruiters. A genuine employer or licensed representative will not ask for secret cash payments.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: How can a Brampton RCIC help a home support worker?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: They can compare current pathways for your job and experience, review job offers, prepare applications and warn you about closed programs. They cannot guarantee a job or PR.

/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.question: Can a Brampton consultant guarantee the outcome of a home support worker PR application?
/immigrate/home-support-worker-pilot.answer: No. IRCC, the IRB or the province makes the decision. A licensed RCIC can assess your situation, prepare a strong application and manage deadlines, but cannot guarantee approval. Avoid anyone who promises a result or asks for payment to 'fix' your case.

/locations/toronto.question: Is my immigration consultant in Toronto really licensed?
/locations/toronto.answer: Verify it yourself. The CICC register lists every licensed RCIC and shows whether the licence is active. Lawyers appear in the law society directory for Ontario. Never rely on a business card or social media page.

/locations/toronto.question: Can I get help from CMG without visiting an office in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: You can. Consultations take place by video or phone, documents are shared securely online and Pankaj Khanna, RCIC (R711256), files your application. Your location in Toronto does not change who handles your case.

/locations/toronto.question: Where should I start with immigration if I live in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: List your status, job, language results and family situation first. Then compare federal options with the OINP. Workers in finance, technology, health care and creative industries often have more routes than they expect, so test them before you pay for an application.

/locations/toronto.question: What are the OINP streams relevant to Toronto residents?
/locations/toronto.answer: Ontario’s former OINP streams for employer offers, human capital, graduates and skilled trades are closed to new applicants. The current Ontario Workforce Priority stream has a qualifying Ontario job-offer pathway and a separate route for eligible self-employed physicians. Check its current criteria and intake; living in Toronto alone does not guarantee a nomination.

/locations/toronto.question: How can someone in Toronto improve their CRS score?
/locations/toronto.answer: Retake language tests for higher bands, add Canadian work experience, finish a credential or earn a nomination from Ontario. Each change has a different value, so a consultant can model the options before you spend money.

/locations/toronto.question: Can graduates of the University of Toronto, Toronto Metropolitan University, York University, Seneca, George Brown and Humber get a post-graduation work permit?
/locations/toronto.answer: Often, but not automatically. The program, school status and your language results all matter, and you must apply on time after receiving your final marks. Confirm eligibility before you commit to a course in Toronto.

/locations/toronto.question: What do couples in Toronto need for spousal sponsorship?
/locations/toronto.answer: Proof of a genuine relationship, identity and civil documents, police certificates and medicals. Your sponsorship file is prepared online, so it makes no difference whether you live in Toronto or another city.

/locations/toronto.question: Can my parents come to visit me in Toronto on a Super Visa?
/locations/toronto.answer: Yes, if you meet the minimum income for your family size and buy Canadian private medical insurance for them. They can then stay with you in Toronto for long visits. Prepare an invitation letter and proof of income.

/locations/toronto.question: How can a Toronto business hire without an LMIA?
/locations/toronto.answer: Some workers qualify under exemptions, such as certain international agreements, intra-company transfers or open permits. Each exemption has its own conditions. Do not assume a worker is exempt without checking.

/locations/toronto.question: What do my relatives need to visit me in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: A valid passport, proof of funds, a clear return plan and, depending on their country, a visitor visa or an eTA. Add your invitation letter and proof of your status in Toronto to the file.

/locations/toronto.question: My application was refused. Can a consultant in Toronto help?
/locations/toronto.answer: A consultant can read the refusal letter and officer notes to find the reasons, then advise on reapplying, requesting reconsideration or other options. Deadlines can be short, so act quickly.

/locations/toronto.question: Do trips outside Canada affect my citizenship application in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: Absences reduce the days you can count, so track every trip. Time abroad can delay your eligibility date. Keep passports and travel records, since officers may ask for them.

/locations/toronto.question: Can I book an online meeting from Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: Yes. Meetings are held online, so you can book from Toronto without travelling. Your consultant explains the fees, the tax for Ontario and the next steps in writing before you commit.

/locations/toronto.question: How can I avoid immigration scams in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: Avoid anyone who guarantees PR, sells job offers or LMIAs, or asks for cash without a receipt. Verify the licence on the CICC or law society register and insist on a signed contract.

/locations/toronto.question: What can I realistically expect from a consultant in Toronto?
/locations/toronto.answer: A clear assessment, honest advice, a complete application and timely updates. You should not expect guaranteed approval or shortcuts. If your case is weak, a good consultant will say so.

/locations/mississauga.question: How do I find a licensed immigration consultant in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Check the CICC public register for an active Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant licence, or confirm a lawyer's standing with the law society. Do this before paying anyone for immigration services in Mississauga, because unlicensed agents cannot legally represent you.

/locations/mississauga.question: Does Commonwealth Migration Group serve clients in Mississauga?

/locations/mississauga.question: What are the main routes to PR for workers in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Common routes are Express Entry, the OINP, family sponsorship and employer-supported permits. Which one fits depends on your job, language scores and time in Canada. Local demand in logistics, aviation, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing can help some candidates.

/locations/mississauga.question: Is a Ontario nomination worth pursuing from Mississauga?

The current Ontario Workforce Priority stream has a qualifying Ontario job-offer pathway and a separate route for eligible self-employed physicians. Check its current criteria and intake; living in Mississauga alone does not guarantee a nomination.

/locations/mississauga.question: Does being in Mississauga, Ontario, affect my Express Entry chances?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Not directly. Invitations depend on your score and the draw type. Category-based draws can favour some occupations or French, so check them against your profile instead of your location.

/locations/mississauga.question: Can graduates of the University of Toronto Mississauga and Sheridan College get a post-graduation work permit?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Often, but not automatically. The program, school status and your language results all matter, and you must apply on time after receiving your final marks. Confirm eligibility before you commit to a course in Mississauga.

/locations/mississauga.question: Can I sponsor my spouse if I live in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Yes, if you are a citizen or permanent resident living in Canada and meet the income and relationship rules. The process is federal, so it works the same in Mississauga as it does in the rest of Canada outside Quebec.

/locations/mississauga.question: How long can my parents stay with me in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: A Super Visa can allow long stays on each entry, subject to the terms on the visa. Plan their trips around the insurance coverage and the dates on the visa. Check the current maximum stay before you book.

/locations/mississauga.question: What does an employer in Mississauga need for an LMIA?
/locations/mississauga.answer: A genuine job offer, wage and advertising evidence, and proof the business is real. Processing and wage thresholds vary by province, so check the current rules for Ontario before you recruit.

/locations/mississauga.question: What do my relatives need to visit me in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: A valid passport, proof of funds, a clear return plan and, depending on their country, a visitor visa or an eTA. Add your invitation letter and proof of your status in Mississauga to the file.

/locations/mississauga.question: What should I do first after an IRCC refusal in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Note the date and deadlines, then request the officer's notes if you do not have them. Do not reapply until you understand what went wrong. A representative can review the file with you online.

/locations/mississauga.question: What do I need to become a citizen from Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Proof of physical presence, language results where required, identity documents and a clean eligibility record. After approval you attend a ceremony. Applicants in Mississauga follow the same federal process as everyone.

/locations/mississauga.question: How much does an immigration consultation cost for clients in Mississauga?
/locations/mississauga.answer: Your city alone does not change CMG’s professional fee for a given service scope; the amount depends on the service and the complexity of the file. Applicable tax depends on the place of supply, and government or third-party costs are separate. Ask for a written fee breakdown before proceeding.

/locations/ottawa.question: How do I find a licensed immigration consultant in Ottawa?

/locations/ottawa.question: Does Commonwealth Migration Group serve clients in Ottawa?
/locations/ottawa.answer: Yes. Meetings with CMG are held online, so people in Ottawa and across Ontario get the same service as clients anywhere else. Pankaj Khanna, RCIC, files every case with IRCC and the provinces, whatever your location.

/locations/halifax.question: Who can legally give immigration advice to people in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Only licensed RCICs, lawyers and paralegals in good standing, and Quebec notaries, can charge for immigration advice or representation. Friends, travel agents and recruiters in Halifax cannot, even if they say they have experience.

/locations/halifax.question: Does Commonwealth Migration Group serve clients in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Yes. Meetings with CMG are held online, so people in Halifax and across Nova Scotia get the same service as clients anywhere else. Pankaj Khanna, RCIC, files every case with IRCC and the provinces, whatever your location.

/locations/halifax.question: Which immigration programs suit people living in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Many people in Halifax look at Express Entry, the NSNP, study permit routes and employer-backed work permits. Strengths in ocean technology, health care, defence and education may widen your options. A short consultation can show which route fits your profile.

/locations/halifax.question: Can I apply to the NSNP while living in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Yes, if you meet the current criteria and selection priorities. Since February 18, 2026, Nova Scotia’s four consolidated streams are Nova Scotia Graduate, Skilled Worker, Entrepreneur and Nova Scotia: Express Entry. The province’s Atlantic Immigration Program is a separate federal-provincial pathway. Check current intake and eligibility before applying.

/locations/halifax.question: Will my CRS score differ if I live in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: It will not. Express Entry scores everyone with the same federal formula. A Nova Scotia nomination adds points, and so can some Canadian study or work, but your postal code never does.

/locations/halifax.question: What should international students in Halifax know about study permits and the PGWP?
/locations/halifax.answer: Students at Dalhousie University, Saint Mary's University and Nova Scotia Community College need a valid study permit and, after graduation, may qualify for a PGWP depending on program and school. Rules on eligible fields and language results change, so check before enrolling.

/locations/halifax.question: Can I sponsor my spouse if I live in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Yes, if you are a citizen or permanent resident living in Canada and meet the income and relationship rules. The process is federal, so it works the same in Halifax as it does in the rest of Canada outside Quebec.

/locations/halifax.question: Can my parents come to visit me in Halifax on a Super Visa?
/locations/halifax.answer: Yes, if you meet the minimum income for your family size and buy Canadian private medical insurance for them. They can then stay with you in Halifax for long visits. Prepare an invitation letter and proof of income.

/locations/halifax.question: How can a Halifax business hire without an LMIA?
/locations/halifax.answer: Some workers qualify under exemptions, such as certain international agreements, intra-company transfers or open permits. Each exemption has its own conditions. Do not assume a worker is exempt without checking.

/locations/halifax.question: What do my relatives need to visit me in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: A valid passport, proof of funds, a clear return plan and, depending on their country, a visitor visa or an eTA. Add your invitation letter and proof of your status in Halifax to the file.

/locations/halifax.question: What should I do first after an IRCC refusal in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Note the date and deadlines, then request the officer's notes if you do not have them. Do not reapply until you understand what went wrong. A representative can review the file with you online.

/locations/halifax.question: What do I need to become a citizen from Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Proof of physical presence, language results where required, identity documents and a clean eligibility record. After approval you attend a ceremony. Applicants in Halifax follow the same federal process as everyone.

/locations/halifax.question: Can I book an online meeting from Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Yes. Meetings are held online, so you can book from Halifax without travelling. Your consultant explains the fees, the tax for Nova Scotia and the next steps in writing before you commit.

/locations/halifax.question: How can I avoid immigration scams in Halifax?
/locations/halifax.answer: Avoid anyone who guarantees PR, sells job offers or LMIAs, or asks for cash without a receipt. Verify the licence on the CICC or law society register and insist on a signed contract.

/locations.question: Where does Commonwealth Migration Group help clients with immigration?
/locations.answer: CMG is based in Brampton, Ontario, and serves clients across Canada, including Toronto, Mississauga, Ottawa, Hamilton, London, Kitchener-Waterloo, Windsor, Vancouver, Surrey, Victoria, Kelowna, Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg, Saskatoon, Regina and Halifax. Meetings are online, and Pankaj Khanna, RCIC, files every case, so location does not limit what we can do.

/locations.question: Can I use an immigration consultant in Canada if I live in a different city?
/locations.answer: Yes. A licensed RCIC can represent you anywhere in Canada because federal applications are filed online and handled by IRCC. Provincial programs may add their own steps. Choose a consultant for their licence and experience, not their postal code.

/locations.question: How do I find a licensed immigration consultant in Canada?
/locations.answer: Search the CICC public register for the person's name or licence number, and check that the licence is active. Lawyers can be checked with their provincial law society. Avoid anyone who cannot show a licence.

/locations.question: What is the difference between federal and provincial immigration programs?
/locations.answer: Federal programs, such as Express Entry, are run by IRCC and apply across Canada. Provincial programs, such as the OINP, BC PNP, AAIP, MPNP, SINP and NSNP, let provinces nominate people for local needs. A nomination still needs a federal PR application.

/locations.question: Which province should I choose for immigration to Canada?
/locations.answer: It depends on your occupation, language level, job offers and family ties. Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Nova Scotia all have different streams and priorities. A consultant can compare them against your profile before you commit.

/locations.question: Does my city in Canada affect my Express Entry score?
/locations.answer: No. Express Entry is a federal system and scores everyone with the same formula. A provincial nomination, a job offer or Canadian experience can add points. Where you live does not change the score directly.

/locations.question: Do immigration rules differ between Ontario, British Columbia and Alberta?
/locations.answer: Federal rules are the same everywhere in Canada except Quebec, which has its own selection system. Provincial nominee programs differ in streams, job offer rules and priorities. Check the province before you plan a move.

/locations.question: What if I plan to move to another province after I arrive?
/locations.answer: Provincial nominees are expected to settle in the province that nominated them. Express Entry candidates without a nomination are free to live elsewhere in Canada. Moving soon after a nomination can raise questions, so plan honestly.

/locations.question: Can I get help with study permits and the PGWP from anywhere in Canada?
/locations.answer: Yes. Study permit and PGWP applications are federal and filed online. A licensed consultant can help whether you study in Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Halifax or elsewhere. Check the rules for your school and program first.

/locations.question: Can I sponsor my family from any city in Canada?
/locations.answer: Yes. Spousal and family sponsorship rules are federal, and you can sponsor from any city if you meet the eligibility rules. Quebec has extra requirements. A consultant can check your eligibility and documents.

/locations.question: Can employers in any province hire foreign workers?
/locations.answer: Employers across Canada can apply for LMIAs or use exemptions, subject to wage and sector rules. Requirements and processing differ by province and job. Check the current rules before you hire.

/locations.question: How do online consultations work?
/locations.answer: You book a time by phone or video, share your documents securely and receive written advice. Pankaj Khanna, RCIC, then prepares and files your application online, wherever you live. You get a written fee agreement first.

/locations.question: How much does an immigration consultation cost?
/locations.answer: CMG charges the same fee in every location. Only sales tax changes by province, and government fees are paid separately to IRCC or the province. You will get a written fee agreement before you pay.

/locations.question: How can I avoid immigration scams anywhere in Canada?
/locations.answer: Do not pay anyone who guarantees PR, sells job offers or asks for cash without a receipt. Verify the licence on the CICC or law society register. Report fraud to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

/locations.question: Can an immigration consultant guarantee approval?
/locations.answer: No. IRCC and the provinces make every decision. A licensed consultant can assess eligibility, prepare a strong application and meet deadlines, but cannot guarantee approval. Avoid anyone who does.
